decisions.strongest_defeater: The closed model is consistent with itself; the divergence is between the author text and the declaration semantics that produced the model, i.e., FinishState's HighwayMode-only nesting is a coherent internal reading even though it diverges from the informal requirement description.
decisions.violated_obligation: FinishState's containment must follow the requirement's structure; a transition from another scope (UrbanMode/lane_change_urban) must reach the same FinishState rather than a copy routed through HighwayMode's locally-declared child.

issues.basis: exact_source_inventory.states shows CollisionAvoidanceSystem as a top-level composite (source_id=CollisionAvoidanceSystem, parent=null) matching AutonomousMode's top-level status; canonical_source_ir.initial_states lists CollisionAvoidanceSystem.collision_avoidance_deactive; inspection_equivalent_facts.states marks CollisionAvoidanceSystem/collision_avoidance_deactive/collision_avoidance_active reachable_from_initial=false; verify_facts.non_proved contains matching refuted reachability checks; fcstm_model.text shows only '[*] -> AutonomousMode;' at the outer scope, with no root edge into CollisionAvoidanceSystem.
issues.expected: CollisionAvoidanceSystem's initial pseudostate edge enters collision_avoidance_deactive and this owner-local entry is operationally reachable so the subsystem can actually initialize.
issues.observed: The exact owner-local initial edge [*] -> collision_avoidance_deactive exists at transition:line:76, but CollisionAvoidanceSystem itself (state:CollisionAvoidanceSystem:line:73) has no incoming edge from the root graph (only `[*] -> AutonomousMode;` exists at the outer scope); inspection_equivalent_facts marks CollisionAvoidanceSystem, collision_avoidance_deactive, and collision_avoidance_active as reachable_from_initial=false, and verify_facts refutes reachability for all three (check_id reachability:state:CollisionAvoidanceSystem:line:73, reachability:state:collision_avoidance_deactive:line:74, reachability:state:collision_avoidance_active:line:75).
issues.reason: Per frontier discipline, an owner-level initial-entry contract's satisfaction depends on the entry actually being operationally reachable, not merely syntactically present. The exact deterministic reachability facts show CollisionAvoidanceSystem is a completely isolated composite in the closed FCSTM despite the exact source inventory placing it as a sibling top-level state alongside AutonomousMode with its own declared initial edge. This is a structural contrast between the exact source inventory (which declares CollisionAvoidanceSystem as a first-class top-level composite, parent=null, structurally parallel to AutonomousMode) and the closed model root graph (which only wires [*] -> AutonomousMode), leaving no path to the owner's local initial edge.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The literal owner-local edge target matches the contract's named target exactly (collision_avoidance_deactive), so a narrow reading of only the local S2 initial-entry edge in isolation would consider this satisfied; the defect is the root-level disconnection of the owning composite, not the shape of the local edge itself.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidanceSystem initial entry edge exists locally but owning composite is unreachable from root

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions row for transition:line:76 (source [*], target collision_avoidance_deactive, scope CollisionAvoidanceSystem); inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL for CollisionAvoidanceSystem and collision_avoidance_deactive.
issues.expected: The owner-local initial pseudostate edge CollisionAvoidanceSystem[*] -> collision_avoidance_deactive must actually initialize the subsystem into a reachable, operating state.
issues.observed: The exact edge transition:line:76 ([*] -> collision_avoidance_deactive, scope CollisionAvoidanceSystem) exists and targets the correct state, but CollisionAvoidanceSystem itself is not reached from any top-level initial entry, so this local initial edge never fires in practice.
issues.reason: The initial-entry edge itself is correctly formed (source=[*] owned by CollisionAvoidanceSystem, target=collision_avoidance_deactive), so per protocol this exact contract should be treated as satisfied at its own semantic layer; it is included here only to make explicit that predicate S2 support for the edge does not extend to guaranteeing operational entry, and the root reachability defect is captured separately in the derived contract.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The owner-local edge is syntactically well-formed and targets the exact required child state; per the converse owner rule, a satisfied owner-local initial edge should not be turned into a violation merely because the owner is unreachable — that defect belongs to the owner's root-reachability obligation, not this initial-entry contract.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidanceSystem-local initial entry exists but is structurally unreachable from root

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers row for event pedestrian_detected_dist_to_rear_5_vel_30_dist_to_front_15_high_way_true_dist_to_front_10_urban_way_true (reachable_consumer_state_refs=[], reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]); inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for the same event; verify_facts.checks non_proved row event-consumer:pedestrian_detected... status=refuted.
issues.expected: The activation event (pedestrian/rear/front danger conditions) must be operationally consumable while the vehicle operates in either HighwayMode or UrbanMode, since the guard explicitly references highway/urban distinctions.
issues.observed: The declared consumer transition (transition:line:77, collision_avoidance_deactive -> collision_avoidance_active) exists, but inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers reports reachable_consumer_state_refs=[] and reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] for this event; verify_facts confirms event-consumer check status=refuted because collision_avoidance_deactive/active are unreachable from the top-level initial entry.
issues.reason: NL12 requires the danger-detection conditions be evaluated regardless of HighwayMode/UrbanMode context, i.e. operationally, but the deterministic event-consumer facts show declared-but-unreachable consumer coverage, which is the exact narrower-than-required operational coverage this property targets.
issues.requirement_quote: It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met, such as detecting pedestrians (`pedestrian_detected`), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (`dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30`), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The event is declared and its sole intended consumer transition is structurally correct (right source/target/guard-carrying event); if a future top-level entry made CollisionAvoidanceSystem reachable, this exact transition would already correctly consume the event, so the defect is entirely attributable to the upstream reachability gap rather than a wrong-consumer-scope defect in the transition itself.
issues.title: Collision-avoidance activation event has a declared consumer transition but zero reachable consumer in either HighwayMode or UrbanMode scope

issues.basis: fcstm_model.text FinishState -> [*] : /auto_finished_true effect { R45RouteToken = 20; }; and HighwayMode -> HighwayMode : if [R45RouteToken == 20]; inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions rows transition:line:36 (FinishState->[*], effect R45RouteToken=20) and transition:line:65 (HighwayMode->HighwayMode, guard R45RouteToken==20, reachable_from_initial=true); reference_inspection_facts diagnostic I_TRANSITION_TO_SELF_VIA_PARENT at line 65 confirming this self-loop crosses the composite.
issues.expected: Once HighwayMode transitions to FinishState under auto_finished=true, the system must reach stable completion at FinishState (i.e., FinishState should function as a genuine terminal/ending point for the driving scenario).
issues.observed: FinishState is not a terminal sink: the enclosing AutonomousMode scope contains transitions HighwayMode->HighwayMode (guard R45RouteToken==20) and UrbanMode->HighwayMode (guard R45RouteToken==21) that are set by the very auto_finished_true-triggered transitions ending in FinishState (transitions at lines 33-36, 55-58 set R45RouteToken=20/21 and target [*], which resolves through FinishState-entry sub-transitions at lines 23-25 and back out through the AutonomousMode-level routing transitions at lines 65-66). This means completion at FinishState under auto_finished=true is followed by continued operation (re-entry into HighwayMode) rather than stable termination.
issues.reason: Per the explicit lens instruction to audit every termination contract's target ancestry and continuations, the FCSTM's compiler-generated routing shows FinishState is embedded in a cycle (FinishState -> [*] with R45RouteToken=20 -> HighwayMode->HighwayMode using that same token) rather than being a stable terminal state, which directly violates the must_terminate/not_completed obligation even though the literal endpoint transition into FinishState is present.
issues.requirement_quote: The HighwayMode ends when the system transitions to FinishState, triggered by the `auto_finished=true` condition.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The literal endpoint edge into FinishState (HighwayMode -> FinishState on auto_finished=true) exists and is exactly bound (tr_0020/tr_0009/tr_0011/tr_0032 family), so one could argue the NL6 obligation is only about that single edge's existence, which is satisfied; however per the explicit termination-audit instruction, endpoint existence alone does not establish stable completion when the named ending target routes back into continued operating behavior.
issues.title: FinishState does not achieve stable completion: it re-routes back into HighwayMode/UrbanMode via the compiler route-token mechanism

issues.basis: fcstm_model.text UrbanMode auto_finished_true transitions (lines 55-58) setting R45RouteToken=21 and AutonomousMode-level transition UrbanMode -> HighwayMode : if [R45RouteToken == 21] (line 66); inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions rows transition:line:57/58 (effects R45RouteToken=21) and transition:line:66 (UrbanMode->HighwayMode, guard R45RouteToken==21, reachable_from_initial=true).
issues.expected: Once UrbanMode transitions to FinishState under auto_finished=true, the system must reach stable completion at FinishState.
issues.observed: The UrbanMode auto_finished_true-triggered transitions (lines 55-58) set R45RouteToken=21 and route through FinishState-entry sub-transition at line 25 and back out through the AutonomousMode-level transition at line 66 (UrbanMode -> HighwayMode, guard R45RouteToken==21), continuing operation into HighwayMode rather than terminating.
issues.reason: Symmetric to the HighwayMode case (NL-CONTRACT-REF-018/NL6-TERMINATION-1), the UrbanMode completion path also loops back into HighwayMode via the compiler route-token mechanism rather than achieving stable completion at FinishState, per the explicit termination-audit instruction to inspect all target/active-ancestor continuations.
issues.requirement_quote: The system exits the UrbanMode state by transitioning to FinishState once `auto_finished=true` is satisfied.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The literal UrbanMode -> FinishState edge on auto_finished=true exists and is exactly bound, satisfying a narrow endpoint-only reading of the obligation.
issues.title: UrbanMode's completion at FinishState also fails stable termination via the same route-token cycle

issues.basis: fcstm_model.text root scope containing only [*] -> AutonomousMode (line corresponds to transition:line:80) with no edge into CollisionAvoidanceSystem; inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL rows for state:CollisionAvoidanceSystem:line:73, state:collision_avoidance_deactive:line:74, state:collision_avoidance_active:line:75; verify_facts.checks non_proved reachability rows for the same three states (status=refuted).
issues.expected: CollisionAvoidanceSystem, an independently required operating subsystem, must be reachable from the model's root-level initial entry so its activation/deactivation behavior can ever execute.
issues.observed: The root scope's only initial edge targets AutonomousMode (transition:line:80, [*] -> AutonomousMode); no transition anywhere in the closed model enters CollisionAvoidanceSystem or any of its substates from a reachable state. inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics reports STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL for CollisionAvoidanceSystem, collision_avoidance_deactive, and collision_avoidance_active; verify_facts confirms all three reachability checks as refuted.
issues.reason: NL12/NL13 describe an independently initialized, continuously operating subsystem coupled to conditions from both HighwayMode and UrbanMode, implying it must actually run; the deterministic closed-model facts show it is completely isolated from the reachable state graph, which is a root-reachability defect distinct from and prior to the owner-local initial-entry and event-consumer-coverage defects.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: CollisionAvoidanceSystem may be intended as a structurally separate top-level region documented outside the AutonomousMode hierarchy, and PlantUML/source syntax alone cannot force concurrent-region semantics; if the modeling intent is that this subsystem is a logically independent, always-active monitor rather than one reached via a discrete transition, root reachability in the sequential-state sense may not be the intended semantics — however the closed model provides no such concurrent-region construct, so the sole avenue for CollisionAvoidanceSystem to ever operate is a reachable initial edge, which is absent.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidanceSystem operating scope is unreachable from the root/top-level initial entry

branches.reason: This lens audits contract completeness, containment/owner default-entry structure, transition-group guard collisions, and cross-context consistency for the closed FCSTM against the exact PlantUML/canonical source. Key finding: the CollisionAvoidanceSystem composite and its two child states have no root-level default entry path connecting them to the reachable root graph. The closed FCSTM shows [*] -> AutonomousMode at root but no root/system-level edge into CollisionAvoidanceSystem, even though exact_source_inventory declares CollisionAvoidanceSystem as a first-class top-level composite parented at null, exactly like AutonomousMode. This makes the entire subsystem, its owner-local initial pseudostate edge (line 76: [*] -> collision_avoidance_deactive), and its two transitions structurally isolated from root reachability. I checked the other candidate loci: NL3-INITENTRY-1/NL7-INITENTRY-1 owner-local edges (lines 26/47) correctly target enter_hwy/enter_urban and are reachable, so they are satisfied and omitted; the INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL diagnostics on lines 23-25 concern compiler-generated route-token segments for HighwayMode/UrbanMode's own [*]->FinishState routing (unrelated to NL3/NL7's contained-entry contracts) and do not defeat those satisfied contracts; NL3-DISJOINT-1 is satisfied because enter_hwy's two exact triggers (dist_to_front_25 vs dist_to_front_25_extra_lane_true) are disjoint in the closed model, so it is omitted; NL1-DERIVED root entry into AutonomousMode is satisfied via transition:line:80, so it is omitted. I emit one candidate against the CollisionAvoidanceSystem owner-local initial_entry contract (NL-CONTRACT-REF-037) capturing the exact structural disconnection, since the owner-local edge exists but the owning scope itself is disconnected from root reachability, a genuine structural/contrastive defect distinct from the endpoint-existence property of NL12/NL13's transitions (which retain their own event_consumer_coverage/endpoint properties independently).
